analysis:
Examined all units. Most changes are model-free test scaffolding: PlacementChecks/Main.swift calls a new checkGemmaTensorParallel; run.sh adds Gemma4TensorParallelPlan, QwenTensorParallelLaunch and Gemma4TensorParallelRequestBudget to the compile list; the new Gemma plan check and gemma-run.sh read only local safetensors headers and config. They use no network and no model execution, and write only to an mktemp directory removed by a trap, so I found no new attack surface. The plan check also asserts that vision, unknown and misaligned tensors are refused, which is a positive control.

The security-relevant source change is DistributedResidentExecution.swift lines 78-90 (head 79-88). The inline logprob capability predicate (tensorParallel mode AND (GLM5 adapter OR Qwen tensor lanes)) is replaced by ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.capturesLogprobs(capability, mode:). That function's source was not supplied. The refusal path at base line 374 gates on supportsLogprobs, so the new policy could widen what is accepted, e.g. to Gemma, or change fail-closed behavior for an unknown adapter. The comment says unknown adapters fail closed, but I could not verify that. Logprobs for an unsupported model would produce a logprobCaptureUnsupported refusal. A broader policy could instead make workers accept requests they cannot serve. This is a correctness and availability concern, not a confidentiality regression I can demonstrate. Integration should confirm that ClusterModelFeaturePolicy defaults to false for unknown adapters and that it matches NativeWorkerRuntime.capturesLogprobs.

The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (7933a0f to a4f67fa) is not reviewable from the supplied evidence. Because MLX inference runs inside the TB-007 process boundary and handles decrypted prompts (A-001), the upstream diff should be reviewed separately. The Gemma4TensorParallelPlan and QwenTensorParallelLaunch sources are not in this batch, so tensor-parallel hand-off security is not assessed. No threat-model IDs are directly violated by what was supplied.
